ai.title: Restore claude cost tracking calculations
ai.summary: Restored claude cost tracking calculations in `backend/src/claude.ts`. Fixed billing.knowledge.md, removing verbose schema details and condensing to core components. Added quota management and subscription status sections to `backend/knowledge.md`. Removed `backend/src/browser-debugging.knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: The assistant's cost tracking was restored so that billing calculations run correctly again when tracking how much each conversation costs. You would notice usage being recorded properly in the backend system, with quota and subscription status now clearly separated so subscribers skip quota limits while still being tracked for billing, and the old verbose billing documentation was trimmed down to core information.

ai.title: Fix tool call stream processing logic
ai.summary: Refactors `processStreamWithTags` in `backend/src/process-stream.ts` to handle stream completion correctly. Replaces `break` with `continue` inside the chunk loop to prevent premature exit before final buffer parsing. Ensures all chunks are processed even after `streamCompleted` flag is set.

eli5.text: When the assistant is finishing a response, the system now keeps reading incoming data until it has caught the very last piece, instead of stopping early when it thinks the response is done. This prevents the final portion of a streamed answer from being cut off or skipped. If you are watching a response stream in real time, you should now get the complete message every time. It is a behind-the-scenes fix and does not change what features are available.

ai.title: Rename plancomplexchange to thinkdeeply
ai.summary: Tool renamed from `plan_complex_change` to `think_deeply`. Logic updated in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to track recent thinking via user messages. `backend/src/planning.ts` now offers choice between direct implementation or writing markdown plans.

eli5.text: The assistant's planning tool, previously known as 'plan_complex change', has been renamed to 'think deeply' to better reflect its purpose. When you ask the assistant to handle something complex, it now tracks your recent thinking activity to decide whether to implement changes directly or write out a detailed markdown plan first. The system prompt and planning instructions have been updated to guide the assistant toward choosing the most appropriate approach based on your request. This change is live today and affects how internal planning and implementation decisions are made behind the scenes.

ai.title: Adjust new file check prompt
ai.summary: Modified prompt in `backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts` to bias towards reading more files when current context is sparse (e.g., only knowledge files). This aims to prevent under-reading when initial context is low.

eli5.text: The assistant now reads more files when it has very little context at the start of a task, especially if only background knowledge files are loaded. This means fewer chances of the assistant missing important information because it didn't look at enough files. If you watched the system work, you'd notice it picking up additional relevant files in cases where it previously would have stopped too soon. This change is live today and affects how thoroughly the assistant gathers information before answering.

ai.title: Claude fallback for relevant-files planning
ai.summary: backend/src/planning.ts wraps the gemini2flash relevant-files prompt in try/catch and routes failures to promptClaude. Triggered when Gemini throws, logged via logger.warn as a fallback path. Scope is the planning subsystem only. Cost mode selects the fallback model: lite uses claudeModels.haiku, otherwise claudeModels.sonnet, with the same system prompt passed through the system option.

eli5.text: When the system tries to figure out which files are relevant to a user's request, it first asks a primary AI helper. If that helper fails to respond, it now automatically tries a second AI helper instead of stopping and showing an error. The second helper is chosen based on whether the system is running in a budget mode or not: a faster, cheaper option for budget mode and a more thorough option otherwise. This only affects the initial file-gathering step in the planning process, and you as a user would simply notice that it keeps working even when one of the AI services has a problem.

ai.title: Relace AI fallback to Gemini Flash 2.0
ai.summary: Adds fallback to Gemini Flash 2.0 when Relace AI fails. Refactors newline handling: Relace now appends '\n' before return, while fastRewrite stops appending it. This ensures consistent output formatting across primary and fallback paths.

eli5.text: If the main assistant that rewrites your code fails to respond, the system can now automatically try a different assistant named Gemini Flash to get the job done instead of giving up. When this backup kicks in, you'll notice the rewritten code ends with a line break just like before, so your files stay neatly formatted either way. This works today for anyone using the code-rewriting feature.

ai.title: Update docs for model types
ai.summary: Updated `web/src/content/advanced/what-models.mdx` to reflect current model usage. Replaced references to `Claude 3.5 Haiku` and `o1` with `Gemini Flash` and `o3-mini`. Updated `--max` and `--lite` mode descriptions to clarify file pulling behavior and cost ratios.

eli5.text: The public documentation that describes which AI models the tool uses has been updated to match the models it actually relies on right now. If you read the docs, you will see that the helper used to search your files is now described as Gemini Flash instead of Claude 3.5 Haiku, and the model used for difficult reasoning tasks is now listed as o3-mini instead of o1; the descriptions of the two optional modes were also rewritten so that the lower-cost mode is said to use Claude 3.5 Haiku for edits and the higher-performance mode is said to pull in more files for broader context, while a fallback service for fast file rewrites is now named Relace AI. This is a behind-the-scenes documentation correction only: no code or behavior changed, and you would notice the difference only if you happened

ai.title: Route Gemini Vertex through Helicone gateway
ai.summary: Gemini Vertex backend routes requests through Helicone gateway. VertexAI instance configures apiEndpoint to gateway.helicone.ai and injects Helicone-Auth and Helicone-Target-URL headers. RequestOptions passed to getGenerativeModel apply customHeaders. Affects backend/src/gemini-vertex-api.ts.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant with the Gemini model through our internal backend, your requests now travel through a Helicone gateway on their way to Google Vertex AI, so the calls are still live and working today but they pass through an extra routing layer for logging or observability. If you looked at the system, you'd see the backend is pointed at a gateway address instead of talking directly to Google's servers, and it carries Helicone authentication headers with each request. This affects the internal backend that serves Gemini responses, so end users just get a response the same way, while the operations team now has a traceable path for those requests.

ai.title: Gemini API timeout added to promptGemini
ai.summary: Added timeout handling to `promptGemini` in `backend/src/gemini-api.ts` using `Promise.race` against a new `timeoutPromise` helper. Timeout is 30s for `geminiModels.gemini2flash`, 200s otherwise. Imports `geminiModels` from `common/constants` for model check.

eli5.text: When the system asks AI for help answering your question, it used to wait forever if the AI stalled. Now it gives up after 20 seconds for quick answers or 3 minutes for longer ones. If you use this service you would notice it stops hanging when the AI is slow and returns a clear error instead of freezing.

ai.title: Allow lazy edits in markdown files
ai.summary: Lazy edit blocks are permitted for new `.md` files in `processFileBlock`. Previously, any new file containing a lazy edit triggered an abort, regardless of extension. Scope: `backend/src/process-file-block.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to create a brand-new Markdown document (like a.md file) that includes a special kind of placeholder edit known as a lazy edit, it no longer aborts and stops the whole task; it now lets those lazy edits through for Markdown files specifically. Previously, any new file containing a lazy edit triggered an abort regardless of file type, so Markdown files with lazy edits would fail silently; only Markdown files benefit, and the change is live today.
